newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PM tells army, interior troops to stay calm.
newsitem.headline: Russia PM tells army, interior troops to stay calm.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Thursday ordered the defence and interior ministers to ensure their troops stay neutral in the latest political crisis, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Tass said Chernomyrdin had asked the ministers and other security chiefs to summon their top officers and explain the "need to stay calm" during a war of words between Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov and security tsar Alexander Lebed.
Tass said Chernomyrdin made the remarks during a meeting of the government after which he intended to brief President Boris Yeltsin in detail over the row between Lebed and Kulikov.
He expressed the hope that the servicemen would "understand everything and sort things out in this situation".
Kulikov said on Wednesday that Lebed had been plotting a "creeping coup" while Yeltsin prepares for heart surgery. Lebed has denied the accusations.

Earlier on Thursday, Chernomyrdin held an extraordinary meeting of top security and defence officials to look into the row. He later told the cabinet that some of Kulikov's comments were justified but dismissed his allegations that Lebed was plotting a mutiny or a coup d'etat.
